title: Effective fppf descent for relative finite Hilbert groupoids
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of stacks in groupoids on the big fppf site $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Here isomorphism presheaves are fppf sheaves and object descent for fppf coverings is effective. For each integer $d\geq1$, form the category fibred in groupoids $\mathcal H_d(F)$ [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]: its objects over $T$ are $(Z\to T,y,x,\alpha)$ with $Z\to T$ finite locally free of degree $d$, $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, $x\in\mathcal X(Z)$ and $\alpha:y|_Z\simeq F(x)$, and its arrows are the compatible cartesian maps and isomorphisms of that definition. Then $\mathcal H_d(F)$ is a stack in groupoids for the fppf topology: all its isomorphism presheaves are sheaves and every fppf descent datum for its objects is effective. No representability, flatness or finite-presentation hypothesis on $F$ is imposed.

proof.text: Pullbacks and groupoid fibres. Use the pullback construction of [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. For $u:T'\to T$, the cover becomes $Z'=Z\times_TT'\to T'$, still finite locally free of degree $d$ by [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-fppf-descent]. Pull back $y$, $x$ and $\alpha$ along $u$ and $Z'\to Z$; the pullback comparison of the morphism of stacks $F$ gives the required isomorphism over $Z'$. The cartesian universal properties in the two given fibred groupoids and of the scheme fibre product give the cartesian lift of the quadruple. Its uniqueness follows component by component from those same universal properties. In a fibre, the scheme map is an isomorphism and both object maps are isomorphisms; their inverses satisfy the compatibility equation by inverting it. Thus this is a category fibred in groupoids.

Descent of the scheme and target components of an arrow. Fix $\xi=(Z/T,y,x,\alpha)$ and $\xi'=(Z'/T,y',x',\alpha')$. On any fppf cover $\{T_i\to T\}$, compatible local isomorphisms $\xi|_{T_i}\to\xi'|_{T_i}$ have components $(g_i,b_i,a_i)$. By the isomorphism-descent clause of [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-fppf-descent], the $g_i$ glue to a unique $T$-isomorphism $g:Z\to Z'$. The $b_i$ glue to a unique $b:y\xrightarrow{\sim}y'$ because $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal Y}(y,y')$ is a sheaf by the hypothesis on $\mathcal Y$. This argument works after every base change $V\to T$, so it checks the isomorphism presheaf on its entire slice site.

Finish descent of arrows. Put $Z_i=Z\times_TT_i$; these form an fppf cover of $Z$ by the base-change covering axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. With $g$ fixed in the previous step, the $a_i$ are compatible sections of $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal X}(x,g^*x')$ on this cover. The stack hypothesis on $\mathcal X$ gives a unique glued isomorphism $a:x\xrightarrow{\sim}g^*x'$. The two sides of the arrow condition $F(a)\circ\alpha=(g^*\alpha')\circ(b|_Z)$ are sections of the same isomorphism sheaf in $\mathcal Y$ over $Z$. They agree on every $Z_i$ by the local arrow condition, hence agree on $Z$. Thus $(g,b,a)$ is an arrow, unique because all three components are unique. Consequently every isomorphism presheaf of $\mathcal H_d(F)$ is an fppf sheaf.

Descend the underlying finite cover of an object datum. Let $\xi_i=(Z_i/T_i,y_i,x_i,\alpha_i)$ and $\varphi_{ij}:\xi_i|_{T_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\xi_j|_{T_{ij}}$ be descent data, where $T_{ij}=T_i\times_TT_j$ and $\varphi_{jk}\varphi_{ij}=\varphi_{ik}$ on triple overlaps. Forgetting the other components gives scheme isomorphisms $\theta_{ij}$ with the same cocycle identity. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-fppf-descent] to obtain $Z\to T$ finite locally free of degree $d$ and isomorphisms $\rho_i:Z\times_TT_i\xrightarrow{\sim}Z_i$ inducing exactly $\theta_{ij}$. Use these isomorphisms to regard all $x_i$ and $\alpha_i$ on the fixed pullbacks of $Z$. In particular all the overlap and triple-overlap schemes are now $Z\times_TT_{ij}$ and $Z\times_TT_{ijk}$; the scheme part of the cocycle supplies these identifications, rather than an identification of $Z_i\times_TZ_j$ with them.

Descend the two objects. Write $b_{ij}$ for the $\mathcal Y$-component of $\varphi_{ij}$ and $a_{ij}$ for its $\mathcal X$-component after the identifications of step 4. Projecting the cocycle equation gives $b_{jk}b_{ij}=b_{ik}$ on $T_{ijk}$. Effectiveness for the given fppf stack $\mathcal Y$ gives $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$ and $b_i:y|_{T_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}y_i$ with $b_j=b_{ij}b_i$. The family $\{Z\times_TT_i\to Z\}$ is an fppf covering by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Its double and triple overlaps are $Z\times_TT_{ij}$ and $Z\times_TT_{ijk}$. The remaining component of the original cocycle is therefore precisely descent data $a_{jk}a_{ij}=a_{ik}$ for the $x_i$ on this cover. Effectiveness for $\mathcal X$ gives $x\in\mathcal X(Z)$ and $a_i:x|_{Z_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_i$ with $a_j=a_{ij}a_i$, where $Z_i$ now denotes the identified pullback.

Glue the comparison and verify effectiveness. All formulas below use the canonical pullback comparisons of $F$. On $Z_i$ define $\widetilde\alpha_i=F(a_i)^{-1}\circ\alpha_i\circ(b_i|_{Z_i})$, an isomorphism from $(y|_Z)|_{Z_i}$ to $F(x)|_{Z_i}$. On $Z\times_TT_{ij}$ the arrow condition for $\varphi_{ij}$ is $F(a_{ij})\alpha_i=\alpha_j(b_{ij}|_Z)$. Using the equations of step 5 gives
$\widetilde\alpha_j=F(a_i)^{-1}F(a_{ij})^{-1}\alpha_j(b_{ij}|_Z)(b_i|_Z)=F(a_i)^{-1}\alpha_i(b_i|_Z)=\widetilde\alpha_i$.
Since $\mathcal Y$ is a stack, its isomorphism presheaf glues these sections to $\alpha:y|_Z\xrightarrow{\sim}F(x)$. The quadruple $(Z/T,y,x,\alpha)$ is an object of [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. The equation $F(a_i)\alpha=\alpha_i(b_i|_{Z_i})$ makes $(\rho_i,b_i,a_i)$ local Hilbert isomorphisms, and the identities for $\rho_i,b_i,a_i$ show they induce the original $\varphi_{ij}$. Thus every object descent datum is effective. Together with the arrow sheaf condition and groupoid fibres, this proves the assertion. Only the stack hypotheses on $\mathcal X,\mathcal Y$ and cartesian functoriality of $F$ have been used.
